findings.title: Ambiguous host launch can bypass immediate owner cleanup
findings.evidence: executed-controller.js.txt:8 rejects any exec_command result with session_id. Lines 20-23 consume the --start and listener results; launchedMeta is parsed and launched becomes true only at line 21. Catch cleanup at lines 63-64 runs guard --abort only when launched is true.
findings.effect: If --start creates the child but the host tool returns a session_id or truncated/non-JSON output, the controller cannot establish launch metadata, does not wait or close that host session, and skips --abort. The guard watchdog is only a later fallback. A child-created synthetic fixture in lifecycle-regression.cjs is expected to expose this path; it is not evidence that the retained attempt hit it.
findings.confidence: Source-order fact; injected execution path is pending parent run.

findings.title: Tool callbacks do not have a controller-wide deadline or cancellation path
findings.evidence: executed-controller.js.txt:17 awaits start_session without a timeout argument. Line 13 passes a per-command timeout to batch_commands but awaits its Promise without an outer deadline. Lines 63-64 and 68-69 await cleanup/final writes without phase checks. A never-resolving awaited call prevents catch/finally completion.
findings.effect: The configured 60-second phase bound does not bound the whole controller when a tool call never resolves. Parent source inspection of the pinned gdb.py reports create at lines 219-259: subprocess creation, a 15-second banner wait, three setup commands with 30-second defaults, and _sessions registration only after setup at line 258. A failure before registration can leave a GDB process without a returned/registered session ID. This is an external ownership/deadline dependency, not fixable by a JavaScript Promise.race alone.
findings.confidence: Controller await behavior is source-confirmed. Service details are attributed to the parent read of the pinned installed gdb.py; no service source was changed or executed.
findings.test: gdb_start_session_never_returns, gdb_callback_never_returns, cleanup_stop_session_never_returns, and host_wait_write_stdin_never_returns use unresolved mocked Promises. The fake clock advances to 60 seconds from that phase's start; the R-T case records and uses the `--handoff` epoch. The mock does not cancel the underlying Promise or model service-side partial process creation.

findings.title: Cleanup responses are recorded but not validated
findings.evidence: executed-controller.js.txt:63 records the --abort exec_command response without checking exit_code. Line 64 records stop_session and clears sid without checking isError or stopped:true. The success cleanup at line 54 likewise clears sid after any resolved stop_session result.
findings.effect: A nonzero abort response or stopped:false can still produce and print SETUP_REJECTED without a cleanup-failed state. The actual retained response was successful and independent post-run inspection confirmed cleanup; the risk is an unhandled negative response, not a failure in the observed attempt.
findings.confidence: Source-order fact; negative envelopes are injected offline.

findings.title: Final evidence writes can overwrite or fail without changing the reported result
findings.evidence: executed-controller.js.txt:16 writes the fixed attempt path; lines 67-69 write the fixed result and transcript paths through PowerShell WriteAllText. The final exec_command response is passed to text() without checking exit_code, and no exclusive-create or prior-hash check is present.
findings.effect: A later invocation rejected by the guard's one-shot check can still overwrite the previous execution result and transcript in finally. A failed final write can leave only an in-memory result while the controller prints it as if evidence finalization completed. The guard's one-shot check at stutter-runtime-guard.py.txt:468-473 protects runtime state/dump inputs, not these controller evidence outputs.
findings.confidence: Source-order fact; final-write and one-shot negatives are injected offline.

findings.title: Architecture admission can accept a structured error that echoes m6809
findings.evidence: executed-controller.js.txt:11 classifies errors with a small text-pattern regex plus top-level isError. Lines 19-20 then accept any serialized configuration response containing m6809.
findings.effect: An envelope with isError:false, structuredContent.error:true, and an echoed m6809 string is not rejected by errorResult and satisfies the substring check, so the controller can reach --start without a successful architecture query. The synthetic case is an injected counterexample; no such error occurred in the retained transcript.
findings.confidence: Static predicate analysis; parent response review separately owns parser characterization.

findings.title: Guard CLI has partial-artifact and exceptional-cleanup boundaries
findings.evidence: stutter-runtime-guard.py.txt:473-478 creates DUMPS and STATE before the guarded Popen try block at line 482. Lines 493-499 perform cleanup inside the exception handler. _cleanup_spawned at lines 392-401 can propagate a second TimeoutExpired. The outer handler at lines 579-581 catches Rejected, OSError, ValueError, and KeyError, not every cleanup exception. Handoff creates HANDOFF before updating STATE at lines 566-569.
findings.effect: A state-write failure before Popen can leave one-shot artifacts. A cleanup exception can prevent the intended SETUP_REJECTED record or escape the listed handler. If HANDOFF creation succeeds and the subsequent state update fails, the handoff file persists and blocks another --start. These are source-only exception-path risks; the guard CLI was not executed.
findings.confidence: Static source review only; no claim that these failures occurred.

findings.title: PID reuse and one-shot runtime-state guards are present
findings.evidence: stutter-runtime-guard.py.txt:318-338 binds process identity to PID, executable, argv, and start_ticks. Lines 368-386 signal only an exact matching process and record identity mismatch without killing it. Lines 468-472 reject an existing STATE, LOG, HANDOFF, or DUMPS artifact. LIMITS at lines 41-43 set attempts to one.
findings.effect: These guard checks are useful protections in the Python CLI, but the offline controller VM does not execute or qualify them. They do not prevent the controller's fixed evidence paths from being overwritten.

findings.title: Stale handoff is rejected before trace admission
findings.evidence: stutter-runtime-guard.py.txt:298-315 enforces B080 identity, one handoff, and a maximum 1000 ms freshness bound. executed-controller.js.txt:51-54 records a fresh R-T epoch, invokes --handoff, and sets handoff=true only after shell returns successfully.
findings.effect: The offline late-handoff fixture should produce an R-T setup rejection and abort without running analysis. This is a protective behavior, conditional on the mocked guard response and not an end-to-end guard result.

findings.title: STARTED acknowledgement metadata is not validated before R-I admission
findings.evidence: executed-controller.js.txt:18-21 extracts the session and accepts launch metadata based only on status === STARTED; the listener state is parsed at lines 22-23, but no PID/start_ticks cross-check occurs. The handoff at lines 51-53 later interpolates launchedMeta.pid and launchedMeta.start_ticks.
findings.effect: A STARTED response with missing or contradictory process identity metadata can proceed through all identity checkpoints and record IDENTITY_PASS before a later handoff rejection. The mock scenario demonstrates the missing-field path with a synthetic guard rejection; it does not establish a live guard response or owner identity.
findings.confidence: Static source fact; conditional controller-flow characterization only.

guard_cli_review.phase_budget: stutter-runtime-guard.py.txt:288-315 enforces 52-second work and 60-second phase limits for guard identity/handoff state. The controller's tool awaits and finalization are outside that local guard's cancellation authority.
guard_cli_review.process_ownership: The guard compares PID/exe/argv/start_ticks and only signals the exact owner. The controller does not itself verify the result of abort/stop_session cleanup.
guard_cli_review.retry: The controller does not contain an automatic R-I/R-T retry loop. The guard rejects existing state/log/handoff/dumps on --start. A repeated controller invocation can nevertheless rewrite fixed controller evidence paths before/after the guard rejection.
guard_cli_review.partial_launch: The guard's Popen cleanup covers exceptions after entering its try block, while the JS controller's ambiguous exec_command/session response can fail before its launched flag is set. These are distinct layers and neither is exercised by a mock-only VM as an integrated path.
guard_cli_review.handoff: Guard handoff writes HANDOFF then updates STATE; partial persistence is fail-closed for subsequent --start but leaves stale one-shot evidence requiring review.
